Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

The $4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02733 is refunded to the rider in full.

For the driver: your case starts from a correct proposition. The rider cancelled the trip herself at 07:55:21, 420 seconds after the 07:48:21 acceptance, so the 180-second grace in trip_record.platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec had expired, and under POL-NS-10(f) a rider's own post-grace cancellation is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd ($4.50 on this record) whether or not you had arrived. But the same limb of the same clause refunds the fee in full where the chat_log shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, and that is exactly what this record shows: MSG-02733-001, sent by you at 07:52:21 and read at 07:52:51, reads 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side', and the rider replied 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21 (MSG-02733-002). Your own advocate concedes the point. Your ETA argument does not rescue the fee: the exception turns on your request, not on whether you were running late, and in any event the rider cancelled roughly eight minutes before the 08:03 arrival time quoted to her. Your point that the fare ledger is clean is accepted (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee $4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd $4.50, and EV-FARE-02733 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0), but a correctly computed amount is not a chargeable one.

How to appeal: You may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04). A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Rider advocate8 claim(s), 7 kept

  1. The driver asked the rider to cancel, and the chat log proves it on its face.

    Read the whole claim

    MSG-02733-001, sent by the DRIVER at 2026-08-15T07:52:21+08:00 and read by the rider at 07:52:51, says 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side'. The rider replied 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21 (MSG-02733-002) and the trip was cancelled by the rider at 07:55:21. That is squarely the third exception in POL-NS-10(f) - the driver asked the rider to cancel, and the chat_log shows it. The $4.50 cancellation fee must therefore be refunded to the rider in full, and the rider's own cancellation stops being the operative fact.

    EV-CHAT-02733, EV-TRIP-02733 · POL-NS-10

  2. The charge is labelled a no-show fee, but no limb of POL-NS-01 holds on this record.

    Read the whole claim

    The trip record's event chain runs driver_assigned 07:48:21, driver_en_route 07:48:29, trip_cancelled 07:55:21 - there is no driver 'arrived' event anywhere, so limb (a) fails. The driver's own trace then breaks limb (b): across 49 fixes the driver is never once inside the pickup geofence, and the qualifying in-radius fix count is zero. Where the anchor clause fails, the fee is not chargeable under it.

    EV-TRIP-02733, EV-GPS-02733 · POL-NS-01

  3. Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 independently fails.

    Read the whole claim

    The record shows no boarding event and the trip was terminated with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED - not RIDER_NO_SHOW, not RIDER_UNREACHABLE, not EXCESSIVE_WAIT. A no-show fee cannot be built on a cancellation recorded under the rider's ordinary cancellation code; the mis-selected code is a driver-education item, not a basis for keeping the fee.

    EV-TRIP-02733 · POL-NS-01

  4. POL-NS-02 deems a driver arrived only where at least 3 consecutive fixes, each accurate to 25 m or better, fall inside the arrival radius - 50 m for this STANDARD zone class, read from the fee schedule.

    Read the whole claim

    The driver's trace carries 49 fixes over the window, zero qualifying in-radius fixes, and a minimum distance to the pickup pin of 7000.03 m: the closest he ever came was seven kilometres away. On this trace the driver never arrived, limb (b) of POL-NS-01 fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

    EV-GPS-02733, EV-TRIP-02733 · POL-NS-02

  5. The softer wrong-entrance route cannot rescue this fee either.

    Read the whole claim

    POL-NS-03 exists for a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin; here the driver's minimum distance was 7.0 km, more than seventeen times that ceiling, so the clause is never engaged and nothing about fault allocation between the parties can displace the refund that POL-NS-02 gives the rider.

    EV-GPS-02733, EV-TRIP-02733 · POL-NS-03

  6. The effective in-geofence dwell is zero seconds against the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, STANDARD zone) - a shortfall of 180 seconds, with a longest qualifying run of 0 fixes.

    Read the whole claim

    The driver's recorded speeds across the trace run from 57.2 to 62.9 km/h, which is a driver moving on a road, not a driver holding position at a pickup. The full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable.

Draft 1 - sampled
The $4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02733 is refunded to the rider in full. For the driver: your case starts from a correct proposition. The rider cancelled the trip herself at 07:55:21, 420 seconds after the 07:48:21 acceptance, so the 180-second grace in trip_record.platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec had expired, and under POL-NS-10(f) a rider's own post-grace cancellation is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd ($4.50 on this record) whether or not you had arrived. But the same limb of the same clause refunds the fee in full where the chat_log shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, and that is exactly what this record shows: MSG-02733-001, sent by you at 07:52:21 and read at 07:52:51, reads 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side', and the rider replied 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21 (MSG-02733-002). Your own advocate concedes the point. Your ETA argument does not rescue the fee: the exception turns on your request, not on whether you were running late, and in any event the rider cancelled roughly eight minutes before the 08:03 arrival time quoted to her. Your point that the fare ledger is clean is accepted (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee $4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd $4.50, and EV-FARE-02733 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0), but a correctly computed amount is not a chargeable one. Independently, the no-show foundation fails and would give the rider the same refund. POL-NS-01 requires a driver 'arrived' event (the trip record has none - its event chain is driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled), fixes inside the pickup geofence (the driver's closest approach to the pin is 7,000.03 m, and across 49 fixes he holds 57.2-62.9 km/h with 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes), and a termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT (the record shows RIDER_CANCELLED). POL-NS-02 accordingly also entitles the rider to the full fee back, and POL-NS-03 is not engaged because 7.0 km is far beyond its 400 m ceiling. For the rider: your claims are accepted. The driver's request to cancel is decisive under POL-NS-10(f); the driver never arrived (limbs (a), (b) and (d) of POL-NS-01 all fail); POL-NS-04 need not exonerate you because you win on POL-NS-10(f) regardless; and every artifact this ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so there is no impairment discount. The one absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-02733-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact here and is not relied on: no advisory covers Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3, so POL-NS-06(i) dwell aggregation is unavailable, but the refund does not depend on it. Amount and compensation: $4.50 is refunded, being the contested cancellation-fee line of EV-FARE-02733 and matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd; no waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee $0.00) and none is due, since POL-NS-10(d) bars charging both on one trip. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not, so the anti-farming check never comes into play. No escalation: POL-NS-09 is not triggered - rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3), disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test does not trip - and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect ($4.50) is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so this refund executes automatically.

She cancelled at 07:55:21 — 420 seconds after acceptance, past the 180-second grace_after_match_sec in force — so the fee would prima facie be chargeable under POL-NS-10(f), but the driver-requested-cancellation exception applies and the fee is refunded in full. The DRIVER advocate's own framing is accepted: this was a rider-triggered, post-grace cancellation rather than a driver-terminated no-show, and the refund runs to the cancellation-fee line of $4.50 only. No waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee $0.00) and POL-NS-10(d) bars both on one trip, so nothing beyond $4.50 is returnable. The no-show anchor fails independently as well: POL-NS-01 needs a driver 'arrived' event (none exists), in-geofence presence (the driver's trace carries 0 qualifying in-radius fixes, closest approach 7,000.03 m from the pin) and a termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT — the record reads RIDER_CANCELLED. No escalation trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor; both tracks and the ledger are COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no contradiction; disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles; rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3); and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 0, rate 0.0). Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — the chat log, the trip record and the GPS trace — is at weight 1.0; the only impaired artifact is the MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02733-01 at weight 0.0, which carries no fact this ruling rests on. Draft 4 - parties' positions swapped
Rider and driver: the $4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02733 (EV-FARE-02733, cancellation_fee $4.50, total_charged $4.50, payment_status CHARGED) is refunded to the rider in full. What the record shows. The driver accepted the job at 07:48:21 and set off; at 07:52:21 he messaged the rider, "sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side" (MSG-02733-001, EV-CHAT-02733, read by the rider at 07:52:51). The rider replied "ok cancelling" at 07:53:21 and cancelled the trip at 07:55:21 (EV-TRIP-02733, cancelled_by RIDER, reason code RIDER_CANCELLED). The driver's position, accepted. The driver is right that this was a rider-triggered cancellation made 420 seconds after acceptance, beyond the 180-second grace in trip_record.platform_policy.grace_after_match_sec, and that under POL-NS-10(f) such a cancellation is chargeable at platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, $4.50, "whether or not the driver had arrived". He is also right that the fare ledger is clean: $4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect exists, and his point that the ETA exception is not engaged (the driver was still moving at 57.2-62.9 km/h when the rider cancelled) is accepted. But POL-NS-10(f) carries a further exception, and it decides the case: the fee "is refunded in full where the record shows ... the driver asked the rider to cancel (chat_log)". The chat log shows exactly that, in the driver's own words and timestamp. The driver's advocate concedes this on the record. The refund therefore follows, and it is a full refund of the cancellation-fee line. The rider's no-show route, accepted as far as it goes but not the operative ground. The rider is right that the charge cannot be sustained as a no-show fee: there is no 'arrived' event and no boarding event in the trip record, the termination is recorded as CANCELLED_BY_RIDER / RIDER_CANCELLED rather than a no-show code, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) fail; and the driver's own trace carries 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes with a minimum distance of 7,000.03 m (7.0 km) across 49 fixes, so POL-NS-02 finds no arrival and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails. POL-NS-03 does not change this: it engages only within 400 m of the pin, and the closest the driver came was 7.0 km, so no wrong-entrance outcome - and no POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill - is available. These clauses point the same way as POL-NS-10(f); the fee is refunded because the driver asked for the cancellation, and would also fail as a no-show charge in any event. Claims that do not move the outcome. POL-NS-04 is not needed: the rider's "ok cancelling" message is not a locating or coordinating message and her single rider fix is timed 07:57:11, after the 07:55:21 cancellation, so that clause would not exonerate her on its own tests - but the refund does not depend on it. The POL-NS-06 dwell arithmetic likewise decides nothing here: the disputed $4.50 is a cancellation fee on a rider-cancelled trip, decided under POL-NS-10. Driver compensation. None is payable. POL-NS-10(f) is a full refund of the fee and carries no driver payment, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test is not reached because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied; the POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill route is unavailable for the distance reason above. Escalation and referrals. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles (limb (c)), rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 against the 3 limb (d) requires, the anti-farming check reads driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 0 against completed_trips_30d = 55 (limb (d)), no two admissible artifacts contradict each other (limb (b)), and the deciding fact is not carried solely by an impaired artifact (limb (e)). No clause produces a referral: no arrival marker was tapped, so POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival record does not fire, and POL-NS-01's driver-education referral is confined to a mis-selected reason code on an in-radius arrival, which is not this case. The reason code RIDER_CANCELLED correctly describes a rider cancellation. Impairment and confidence. EV-ADVIS-02733-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); this ruling does not rely on it. The rider's POL-NS-06 dwell claim, which cited that missing artifact without naming its issue code, was discarded at the mechanical check and supports nothing. The deciding fact - that the driver asked the rider to cancel - is carried by the chat log EV-CHAT-02733 at weight 1.0, and the amount by the fare breakdown EV-FARE-02733 at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 policy floor. The monetary effect of $4.50 does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, so it executes automatically. This is a provisional ruling and either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.
